items.stem: An AI writes a SQL query that returns a plausible number. Before reporting it, the analyst should mainly:

options.text: Read the query logic and validate it against known results
options.rationale: Correct: AI queries can contain subtle logic errors producing plausible but wrong numbers.

options.text: Report the number because it looks reasonable
Assume the AI understood the schema perfectly
options.rationale: AI can misread or assume schema details.

options.text: Trust it since it ran without error
options.rationale: Running without error does not mean the logic is correct.

items.explanation: Correct: AI queries can contain subtle logic errors producing plausible but wrong numbers.

items.stem: Which TWO practices support honest communication of AI-assisted analysis? (Select TWO.)

options.text: State the key data limitations and uncertainty
options.rationale: Correct: caveats keep the audience from over-trusting results.
Correct: avoiding false causal claims keeps findings defensible.

options.text: Present every AI-surfaced pattern as a firm conclusion
options.rationale: Patterns can be spurious; overstating them misleads.

options.text: Hide the data quality issues from stakeholders

items.stem: An AI summary reports that two metrics 'move together'. What is the safest interpretation?

options.text: They are correlated, which does not by itself prove one causes the other

options.rationale: Correlation alone does not establish causation.
Correlations can be coincidental or confounded.

options.text: Causation is proven by the AI
options.rationale: AI noting a correlation does not prove causation.
